question: If many voters now ask chatbots about elections, how do we keep their choices truly their own?
reflection: Clear labels on machine-made text and honest answers about candidates can help citizens think for themselves with better information.

one_line: Knowing where text and information come from is becoming a real requirement, as OpenAI watermarks ChatGPT text in Europe and voters turn to chatbots for election advice.

top_stories.title: OpenAI adds hidden watermarks to ChatGPT text
top_stories.what: OpenAI launched an invisible statistical watermark for text from ChatGPT and Codex, on by default for EU users to meet the EU AI Act, though heavy editing reportedly weakens detection a lot.
top_stories.why: Watermarks help with provenance but cannot prove authorship, so universities and agencies still need fair, evidence-based policies on AI-written work.

top_stories.title: One in five US voters consult chatbots on elections
top_stories.what: Voters told NPR they use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini to compare candidates and check claims, while experts warn agreeable answers can reinforce what people already believe.
top_stories.why: How chatbots shape civic choices is a fresh behavioural research question with policy weight.

top_stories.title: AI agents shortlist new magnetic materials in days
top_stories.what: Vals AI reportedly ran about 90 Claude agents through hundreds of simulations and found two candidate materials for room-temperature spin electronics in three days, still unconfirmed in the lab.
top_stories.why: Agent teams running simulations at scale show how research timelines in other fields could shrink.

saudi_lens.text: Reflection AI pitches open models to sovereign nations that want to train on their own data, a model that fits Saudi plans for national AI capability.

idea.title: Chatbots and civic information study
idea.pitch: Test how leading chatbots answer neutral questions about public services and policies in Arabic, and whether answers shift with how the question is framed.
idea.first_step: Write ten paired questions, one neutral and one leading, on the same public topics.

idea_kids.title: Spot the fingerprint activity
idea_kids.pitch: Children write short notes, then a partner hides a secret pattern in word choices, and the class tries to find which notes carry the hidden mark.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare a list of word pairs to use as the secret pattern.
